result.title: Do Better Scores Mean Better Physics? Physics-Grounded Explanations for Sim2Real Neural Operators
result.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 XAI4Science Workshop, Tiny Paper Track
result.summary: Machine-learning surrogates accelerate physical simulation, but lower prediction error need not coincide with lower error in physically relevant flow statistics. We examine this question for flow around a NACA4418 airfoil using paired computational-fluid-dynamics simulations and experimental particle-image-velocimetry measurements. A mean-preserving input intervention removes velocity fluctuations from selected regions of observed flow histories. Across four neural operators, removing fluctuations from the most energetic 10% of valid observed cells changes forecasts more than equal-area random removal. Because the masks are not matched for removed fluctuation energy, this contrast measures sensitivity, not independent evidence of physical importance. Separately, a CNO has lower velocity-field error but substantially higher two-component fluctuation-energy error than the reference on both analysis subsets. An output attenuation stress test also demonstrates disagreement between benchmark errors and domain-summed fluctuation energy. These single-benchmark results motivate reporting complementary physical diagnostics alongside aggregate prediction scores; they do not establish counterfactual physical correctness.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文以 NACA4418 翼型绕流为对象，对比 CFD 与 PIV 数据，通过均值保持的输入干预（去除特定区域速度脉动）和输出衰减压力测试，检验神经算子预测误差与其物理流量统计误差是否一致。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心线索是「聚合分数好≠物理诊断好」及区域输入干预下的因果/敏感度区分，可能启发 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 latent 内容因果贡献的归因设计；但作者明确说明该对比只反映敏感性，迁移到 VLM 推理评价需较多核查。
